standard_prerequisites.name: Bi-invertibility
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map is bi-invertible when it has both a left inverse and a right inverse, and bi-invertibility implies the existence of a quasi-inverse.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the predicate shown to be a mere proposition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractibility of the two inverse types
standard_prerequisites.statement: Under a quasi-inverse both the left inverse type and the right inverse type of the map are contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It makes the product of the two layers contractible.

standard_prerequisites.name: Products of contractible types
standard_prerequisites.statement: A product of contractible types is contractible.

core_obligations: Assume the map bi-invertible and reduce the goal to contractibility of the bi-invertibility structure (source line 398).
Derive a quasi-inverse from bi-invertibility, so that the contractibility result applies to both inverse types (source lines 399-399).
Conclude contractibility of the product of the two inverse types, which is the bi-invertibility structure, from the product case for contractible types (source lines 399-400).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce propositionality to contractibility under an inhabitant.
Get a quasi-inverse, apply contractibility of the inverse types and the product case.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 394-396 (book Theorem 4.3.2): for every map f the type of bi-invertibility structures on f is a mere proposition. The statement is again a propositionality claim, and the proof (source lines 397-400) reduces it to contractibility under an assumed structure, then has to notice that bi-invertibility yields a quasi-inverse, which is the hypothesis needed to apply the contractibility of both inverse types, after which the product case for contractible types finishes the job. The detour through the quasi-inverse is the content and it is invisible in the statement.
